data.narrative:
Palantir is a public-stage AI & Software company currently valued at $312.5B following its public listing. The relevant peer universe comprises 1 public comparable (itself) and 8 private AI & Software companies, including Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. This limited public peer set reflects the nascent maturity of frontier AI infrastructure as a tradeable category.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable to this target. The company's scale, business model, and trajectory differ sufficiently from the identified private peers that applying a median multiple would introduce material distortion. Among 15 same-sector peers screened, none met concurrent stage, revenue scale, or market position criteria required for statistical reliability (minimum threshold: 3 comparable datapoints). A broad sector-wide median would conflate heterogeneous business models and growth profiles inappropriate for triangulation.

The $312.5B current market valuation reflects public market pricing as of the valuation date. Without additional financial metrics—revenue run-rate, EBITDA, user growth, or contract backlog—or a sufficiently dense comparable set meeting screening criteria, traditional multiples-based synthesis cannot be responsibly applied. The key uncertainty remains the appropriate comparability framework for a diversified AI software platform with both government and commercial revenue streams. Further analysis would require either narrower peer selection or introduction of fundamental metrics to anchor valuation.
